Issues.Title: Replace banned APIs in native code
Issues.Body:
## Summary

- replace banned formatted-output APIs in first-party native code with typed C++ streams and string construction
- replace first-party `memcpy` calls with `std::copy_n` and propagate destination capacities so copies are validated before execution
- use `getenv_s` for the diagnostic environment flag on Windows (the old `_dupenv_s` was not banned, but it allocated unnecessarily)
- retain a narrowly scoped `getenv` presence check on Unix, where no better portable replacement is available; the returned pointer is neither dereferenced nor retained
- note that the Windows and Linux implementation behave differently when the variable is set to empty string; I didn't change this to maintain compatibility
- leave vendored third-party code unchanged

## Justification

The replacements remove avoidable banned APIs while preserving existing output and training behavior. Explicit capacity propagation strengthens the copy replacements rather than merely changing the function name. The Unix environment lookup controls only optional diagnostic output and uses `getenv` solely to test whether the variable exists.

> This PR was generated with GitHub Copilot.

Issues.Title: [release/6.0] Backport native dependency installer from #7760
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Partial backport of #7760 to `release/6.0`: add only `eng/install-dependencies.sh`, unchanged from the original PR and preserving its executable bit.

## Why this is needed

Copilot code review uses the setup configuration from `main`, which invokes `sudo ./eng/install-dependencies.sh`, while checking out the PR's code. The wrapper is missing from `release/6.0`, so review setup for #7896 failed before dependency installation:

```text
sudo: './eng/install-dependencies.sh': command not found
```

See the [failure comment](https://github.com/dotnet/machinelearning/pull/7896#issuecomment-6793555710) and [workflow run](https://github.com/dotnet/machinelearning/actions/runs/43004781956).

Adding the wrapper supplies the entry point expected by that setup configuration. It delegates to the existing Arcade dependency installer and adds OpenMP installation.

## Why only this part is backported

The missing wrapper is sufficient to explain and fix this specific setup failure. Its required helper scripts already exist on `release/6.0`; no Arcade update is needed.

The release branch's own setup workflow already installs the Arcade dependencies and `libomp-dev` directly, so changing it is unnecessary for this fix. The remaining documentation, test cleanup, and CI call-site changes from #7760 are unrelated to the missing entry point and would expand the servicing change without helping resolve this failure.

## Validation

- Verified that the script contents exactly match #7760 and that its Git mode is `100755`.
- Confirmed both required helper scripts exist.

> [!NOTE]
> This PR description and backport were prepared with GitHub Copilot.

Issues.Title: Fix non-Latin text encoding for RoBERTa trainers
Issues.Body:
Fixes #7858

## Summary

`EnglishRobertaTokenizer` currently drops input characters that do not map directly to a single byte. That silently removes non-Latin text before the TorchSharp RoBERTa/NAS-BERT trainers see it.

This change encodes characters above Latin-1 as UTF-8 bytes before byte-level BPE, while retaining the existing single-byte mapping for Latin-1 characters so pretrained model token IDs remain stable. Token offsets and partial token-count results continue to refer to UTF-16 positions in the original input.

Regression coverage exercises Korean, Cyrillic, Japanese, supplementary-plane emoji, Latin-1 compatibility, cache reuse, and forward/reverse token limits.

## Validation

- `dotnet test test/Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers.Tests/Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers.Tests.csproj --framework net8.0 --no-restore` — 451 passed.
- Focused `EnglishRobertaTests` run — 10 passed.
- `dotnet build src/Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers/Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers.csproj --framework netstandard2.0 --no-restore` — succeeded with 0 warnings and 0 errors.

Issues.Title: SentencePieceTokenizer (Unigram, from tokenizer.json): equal-score segmentations are ordered differently from Hugging Face tokenizers
Issues.Body:
**System Information:**
 - OS & Version: Debian 13 (trixie), x64
 - ML.NET Version: Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers 3.0.0
 - .NET Version: .NET SDK 10.0.404
 - Reference: Hugging Face `tokenizers` 0.23.3

**Describe the bug**
On repetitive input, several Unigram segmentations can have exactly the same total score: they use the same pieces in a different order. When this happens, `SentencePieceTokenizer` picks a different path than Hugging Face `tokenizers`. The resulting token IDs are a permutation of the expected ones.

Hugging Face (`Unigram::encode_optimized`) keeps the path it finds first when scores are equal. Its final piece therefore starts as early as possible. SentencePiece C++ also differs from Hugging Face here, because it accumulates scores in `float`. So this is a parity issue rather than a single "correct" answer. But a tokenizer created with `CreateFromTokenizerJson` is naturally expected to reproduce the Hugging Face output for that file.

**To Reproduce**
Model: `intfloat/multilingual-e5-small`, revision `614241f622f53c4eeff9890bdc4f31cfecc418b3`, file `onnx/tokenizer.json`.

```csharp
using Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers;

using var stream = File.OpenRead("tokenizer.json");
var tokenizer = SentencePieceTokenizer.CreateFromTokenizerJson(
    stream, addBeginningOfSentence: false, addEndOfSentence: false);

Console.WriteLine(string.Join(", ", tokenizer.EncodeToIds("aaaaaaaaaaaa")));
```

| Input | Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers 3.0.0 | Hugging Face `tokenizers` 0.23.3 |
|---|---|---|
| `"aaaaaaaaaaaa"` | `[10, 83151, 83151, 11]` (`▁a`, `aaaaa`, `aaaaa`, `a`) | `[10, 11, 83151, 83151]` (`▁a`, `a`, `aaaaa`, `aaaaa`) |

**Expected behavior**
When the tokenizer is created from `tokenizer.json`, ties between equal-score segmentations are resolved the way Hugging Face resolves them. Alternatively, an option to choose that behavior.

**Additional context**
On a corpus of 12,600 real-world strings, 247 differ from Hugging Face. In every case it is the same pieces in a different order. Typical triggers are runs such as `0000…`, `────`, `====` and `аааа`. For an embedding model the order matters: cosine similarity between the embeddings of the two ID sequences drops to 0.97 in the worst case (median 0.998). That breaks parity tests that expect ≥ 0.9999.

We reimplemented the Hugging Face Viterbi pass over the library's normalized output in about 100 lines. With it, all 12,600 strings match.

A related normalization bug (control characters becoming `<unk>`) is reported in #7908.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "SentencePieceTokenizer (Unigram, from tokenizer.json): equal-score segmentations are ordered differently from Hugging Face tokenizers" (#7909)

Issues.Title: SentencePieceTokenizer: charsmap entries that map to an empty string are not applied, so control characters become <unk>
Issues.Body:
**System Information:**
 - OS & Version: Debian 13 (trixie), x64
 - ML.NET Version: Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers 3.0.0
 - .NET Version: .NET SDK 10.0.404

**Describe the bug**
The precompiled `nmt_nfkc` charsmap used by SentencePiece Unigram models maps 30 control characters to an empty string, i.e. the normalizer deletes them. `SentencePieceTokenizer` does not apply these entries: the character survives normalization and is encoded as `<unk>`. As a result, token IDs differ from both Hugging Face `tokenizers` and SentencePiece C++ on any text that contains these characters.

The affected code points are U+0001–U+0008, U+000B, U+000E–U+001F, U+007F, U+008F and U+009F.

**To Reproduce**
Model: `intfloat/multilingual-e5-small`, revision `614241f622f53c4eeff9890bdc4f31cfecc418b3`, file `onnx/tokenizer.json`.

```csharp
using Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers;

using var stream = File.OpenRead("tokenizer.json");
var tokenizer = SentencePieceTokenizer.CreateFromTokenizerJson(
    stream, addBeginningOfSentence: false, addEndOfSentence: false);

Console.WriteLine(string.Join(", ", tokenizer.EncodeToIds("a\u0001b")));
Console.WriteLine(string.Join(", ", tokenizer.EncodeToIds("hello\u007Fworld")));
```

| Input | Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers 3.0.0 | Hugging Face `tokenizers` 0.23.3 |
|---|---|---|
| `"a\u0001b"` | `[10, 3, 275]` (`▁a`, `<unk>`, `b`) | `[1563]` (`▁ab`) |
| `"hello\u007Fworld"` | `[33600, 31, 3, 32554]` | `[33600, 31, 32554]` |

**Expected behavior**
Charsmap entries whose replacement is an empty string should delete the matched input, as SentencePiece and Hugging Face do.

**Additional context**
We ran every Unicode scalar value (1,112,063 code points) through the normalizer and compared the result with SentencePiece's own normalization. 1,112,033 match; all 30 differences are the code points listed above. Removing these characters before calling the tokenizer brings the result to 1,112,063 of 1,112,063. The behavior is the same whether the tokenizer is created from `tokenizer.json` or from the `.model` protobuf.

Workaround: strip the 30 code points before encoding.

A related tie-breaking difference is reported in #7909.

Issues.Title: Bump BenchmarkDotNet.Diagnostics.Windows from 0.13.12 to 0.15.8
Issues.Body:
Updated [BenchmarkDotNet.Diagnostics.Windows](https://github.com/dotnet/BenchmarkDotNet) from 0.13.12 to 0.15.8.
Release notes _Sourced from [BenchmarkDotNet.Diagnostics.Windows's releases](https://github.com/dotnet/BenchmarkDotNet/releases)._ ## 0.15.8 This release adds OpenMetrics exporter support for Prometheus-compatible metrics export, improves the Roslyn analyzers with multi-target support and better type checking, and fixes several bugs including process deadlocks and WASM trimming issues. ## Features - Add OpenMetrics exporter for Prometheus-compatible metrics output (#​2801) - Add Job info to DisassemblyDiagnoser report headers to distinguish assemblies when using multiple coreruns (#​2884, fixes #​2573) - Add `NO_COLOR` environment variable support for disabling console colors (#​2870) ## Improvements - Multi-target analyzers with improved type assignability checking using semantic model (#​2866) - Add new analyzer diagnostic BDN1503 for better argument/params validation (#​2865, fixes #​2864) - Use PolySharp for `[DynamicallyAccessedMembers]` attribute polyfill (#​2883) - Refactor to use `AsyncProcessOutputReader` for cleaner process output handling (#​2878) ## Bug Fixes - Fix process deadlock issue when reading process output (#​2877) - Fix WASM generated project being trimmed out (#​2872) - Allow filters to filter out every benchmark from a type without errors (#​2879, fixes #​2860) - Fix unhandled exception when running `BenchmarkRunner.Run()` with arguments on invalid benchmark type (#​2880, fixes #​2724) ## Internal - Update release workflow for analyzers (#​2882) - Improve docs building workflow - Cleanup `#if`-`#endif` preprocessor directives using PolySharp polyfills (#​2881) **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/dotnet/BenchmarkDotNet/compare/v0.15.7...v0.15.8 ## 0.15.7 This release introduces Roslyn analyzers to catch incorrect BenchmarkDotNet usage at compile time, improves .NET Framework version detection, and updates OS detection support. ## Features - Add Roslyn analyzers to detect incorrect usage of BenchmarkDotNet at compile-time (#​2837) - Validates benchmark class structure (public, non-sealed, generic constraints) - Checks `[Arguments]`, `[Params]`, and `[ParamsAllValues]` attribute usage - Verifies `[GenericTypeArguments]` requirements - Ensures only one baseline method per category - Validates `BenchmarkRunner.Run` invocations ## Improvements - Improve .NET Framework version detection by retrieving version from `TargetFrameworkAttribute` (#​2682) - Bump Perfolizer 0.6.0 → 0.6.1, bringing updated Windows and macOS version detection in `OsBrandHelper` ## Bug Fixes - Fix null reference handling and exception logging in `TestCaseFilter` for the test adapter - Fix flaky CI tests by increasing build timeout values (#​2854) ## Internal - Improve release workflow in `release.yaml` **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/dotnet/BenchmarkDotNet/compare/v0.15.6...v0.15.7 ## 0.15.6 ## v0.15.6 This release adds ref struct parameter support for `[ArgumentsSource]`, fixes Native AOT runtime moniker resolution, and upgrades to Perfolizer 0.6.0 with the new Pragmastat statistical engine. ### Features - Add ref struct parameter support for `[ArgumentsSource]` attribute, enabling `Span` and `ReadOnlySpan` parameters (#​2849) ### Bug Fixes - Fix runtime moniker normalization for Native AOT targets (#​2852) ### Improvements - Upgrade to Perfolizer 0.6.0 with Pragmastat statistical engine integration ### Documentation - Add documentation for breaking changes related to disassembler native dependencies (#​2836) ### Internal - Introduce GitHub Actions release workflow **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/dotnet/BenchmarkDotNet/compare/v0.15.5...v0.15.6 ## 0.15.5 This release fixes job naming consistency when using `--runtimes`, clamps histogram bin bounds to avoid confusing negative values, and reduces output directory clutter by filtering unnecessary runtime and satellite assembly files. ## Features - Add custom MSBuild targets to remove unnecessary files from the bin directory (#​2737) - Filters out Capstone native binaries for non-target platforms - Removes satellite assemblies from Microsoft.CodeAnalysis packages ## Bug Fixes - Fix job names consistency between `SimpleJobAttribute` and `--runtimes` CLI option (#​2841) - Jobs now use runtime names as IDs consistently across all runtime monikers - Clamp histogram bin lower bounds to non-negative values (#​1821) - Prevents confusing negative values in histogram output for non-negative measurements ## Internal - Bump Perfolizer: 0.5.3 → 0.5.4 (#​2773) - Update changelog and GitHub Pages generation workflows - Enable `workflow_dispatch` for test workflow (#​2835) **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/dotnet/BenchmarkDotNet/compare/v0.15.4...v0.15.5 ## 0.15.4 This release fixes issues with `ParamsSource` attribute resolution in inheritance scenarios and corrects a MSBuild syntax error in the TestAdapter. ## Bug Fixes - Allow `[ParamsSource]` to resolve overridden methods and properties in derived classes (#​2832) - Fix MSBuild condition syntax for `TestTfmsInParallel` property that prevented Visual Studio from loading projects (#​2831) **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/dotnet/BenchmarkDotNet/compare/v0.15.3...v0.15.4 ## 0.15.3 This release brings .NET 10 NativeAOT instruction set support, improved CPU detection on Windows when WMIC is unavailable, test adapter filtering, and numerous bug fixes. ## Breaking Changes - Deprecated `.WithNuget()` job extension in favor of `.WithMsBuildArguments()` (#​2812) ## Features - Add VS Test Adapter filter support for running specific benchmarks (#​2788) - Update NativeAOT instruction set support for .NET 10+ (#​2828) ## Improvements - Add PowerShell-based CPU detection fallback for Windows when WMIC is unavailable (#​2749) - Improve `IsNetCore` and `IsNativeAOT` detection for single-file apps without AOT (#​2799) - Use `--nodeReuse:false` for dotnet CLI commands to improve build isolation (#​2814) - Enable assembly signing for debug builds (#​2774) ## Bug Fixes - Fix `ArgumentsSource` on external types not working if the argument type is not primitive (#​2820) - Fix workload warmup mode not working correctly - Fix `EtwProfiler` for file paths slightly under 260 characters (#​2808) - Fix console logs being output twice when using TestAdapter (#​2790) - Fix `EventProcessor.OnEndValidationStage` not being called when critical validation errors occur (#​2816) - Fix `XmlException` thrown when `TextReader.Null` is passed to `AppConfigGenerator` (#​2817) - Fix case sensitivity issue in `NativeMemoryLogParser` program name matching (#​2795) - Fix typo in `BuildPlots.R` ## Internal - Replace StyleCop.Analyzers with unstable version for improved analysis (#​2796) - Add workflow to run selected tests (#​2797) - Fix flaky `MemoryDiagnoser` tests on macOS (#​2813) - Fix x86 disassembler tests for net462 (#​2792) - Split `TimeConsumingBenchmark` class to reduce test time - Update `BenchmarkDotNetDiagnosers` package version (#​2805) - Fix comment in package props about `GenerateProgramFile` (#​2802) **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/dotnet/BenchmarkDotNet/compare/v0.15.2...v0.15.3 ## 0.15.2 This release improves memory allocation measurement accuracy and adds new features for job ordering and runtime validation. ## Features - Add `JobOrderPolicy` option to sort jobs in numeric order instead of ordinal order (#​2770) - Add `RuntimeValidator` to detect benchmarks with null runtime configuration (#​2771) ## Improvements - Improve memory diagnoser accuracy with better allocation measurement isolation, warm-up phase, and handling of tiered JIT (#​2562) ## Bug Fixes - Auto-generate unique job IDs between benchmark runs to prevent ID collisions - Skip null runtime validation for in-process toolchain (#​2780) - Fix flaky memory allocation test (#​2782) - Fix benchmark test adapter enumeration issues (#​2766) ## Internal - Modify macOS runner image for CI (#​2775) - Add setting to skip test reports when original workflow is cancelled (#​2772) - Suppress xunit non-serializable data warnings (#​2769) - Enable `--force-clone` for docs-fetch in generate-gh-pages workflow - Allow `workflow_dispatch` for publish-nightly workflow - Enhance docs-fetch command with additional options - Remove `docs/_changelog` folder from main branch (migrated to docs-changelog branch) **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/dotnet/BenchmarkDotNet/compare/v0.15.1...v0.15.2 ## 0.15.1 A maintenance release with improved cross-platform compatibility, a new feature for referencing external types in source attributes, and several bug fixes for ARM CPUs and unsupported operating systems. ## Features - Allow `[ArgumentsSource]` and `[ParamsSource]` to reference methods in other types via new constructor overload: `[ArgumentsSource(typeof(MyClass), nameof(MyClass.Values))]` (#​2748) ## Bug Fixes - Fix WakeLock P/Invoke compatibility with ARM CPUs by refactoring `REASON_CONTEXT` to use proper union structure (#​2745, #​2756) - Fix `Console.CancelKeyPress` crash on platforms that don't support it (Android, iOS, tvOS, WASM) (#​2739, #​2741) - Fix CPU detection crash on unsupported operating systems by returning `CpuInfo.Unknown` (#​2740) - Issues.Title: Microsoft.ML.TorchSharp QuestionAnswer: training takes the answer's last token as inclusive but the decoder cuts the span as exclusive — every answer comes back without its last token (a one-token answer is the empty string)
Issues.Body:
**Package**: Microsoft.ML.TorchSharp 0.23.1 (Microsoft.ML 5.0.x), `mlContext.MulticlassClassification.Trainers.QuestionAnswer(...)`. Related: the NER report #7889 (an off-by-one between what the trainer is taught and what the decoder returns).

**Observed.** Train on 300 synthetic extractive questions (`Where does Leo work?` over `Leo works at Tyrell in Oslo. It opened last year.`, answer `Tyrell`, and `Which city is Tyrell in?`, answer `Oslo`), `maxEpochs` 10; the training loss falls to 0.011. Then answer 60 held-out questions and compare `PredictedAnswer[0]` with the expected text:
- exact matches: 0 of 60;
- empty string: 33; strict prefix of the expected answer (`Ty` for `Tyrell`, `Umb` for `Umbrella`, `Won` for `Wonka`): 27; anything else: 0.

So the span the model finds is right and the decoder cuts its last token.

**Cause** (read from `QATrainer.cs`, not stepped through): training computes the inclusive end `answerEnd = answerIndex + answer.Length - 1` and the target token of that character; the decoder slices `.AsSpan(predictStart - questionLength - 2, predictEnd - predictStart)`, a length that is correct for an exclusive end. A one-token answer (start == end) therefore decodes to the empty string.

**Check that it is the cut and not the model**: train the same data with every answer extended through the first character of the next token (a space has no token — the example is skipped — so extend past the whitespace to the next word's first character) and with a ` .` appended to every passage so the last answer also has a next token: the same trainer then answers 56 of 60 held-out questions exactly (`exact_match` 0.93, `char_f1` 0.96).

**Workaround on our side**: that training-side extension plus the passage padding. Models trained with it would answer one token too long once a release decodes the span the way it trains it.

**Request**: decode the end index as inclusive (`predictEnd - predictStart + 1`) or train an exclusive end, with a test that a model fitted on a trivially learnable one-token-answer set returns its own training answers.

Issues.Title: Microsoft.ML.TorchSharp NamedEntityRecognition: predicted tags come one word to the right (first slot is the start token's, the last word's tag is missing) — a model that tags every word correctly scores as if it had learned nothing
Issues.Body:
**Package**: Microsoft.ML.TorchSharp 0.23.1 (Microsoft.ML 5.0.x), `mlContext.MulticlassClassification.Trainers.NamedEntityRecognition(...)` + `MapKeyToValue("PredictedLabel")`.

**Observed.** Train on 300 short English sentences, one tag per word (6 tags: `B-PER O O B-LOC` for `Alice lives in Paris`, etc.), 10 epochs, then score 50 held-out sentences and compare the `PredictedLabel` vector with the expected tags word by word:

- same position: 0.28 of the words right (macro accuracy over tags 0.09, entity F1 0);
- predicted position = word position + 1: 0.82;
- append one extra word (` .`) to every sentence, drop the first predicted entry, compare: **1.00** of the words, the last word included (the model never saw the extra word in training).

Concretely, `The train from Lisbon arrives at 8 am` (expected `O O O B-LOC O O B-TIME I-TIME`) came back as `O O O O B-LOC O O B-TIME` for the sentence as given — one `O` in front, the last tag (`I-TIME`) missing, the vector length equal to the word count.

**Expected**: the i-th predicted tag belongs to the i-th word, one tag per word.

**Likely cause** (read from `NerTrainer.cs`, not stepped through): training prepends a `0` to the label vector and an init token to the input; `CondenseOutput` writes `prediction[0]` first and then `prediction[i]` for each token that starts with a space, indexing the model output by the encoding index although the model input has the init token in front, so each word receives the prediction of the position before it. The first word has no space prefix, so the output has word-count entries and the final word's own position is never read.

**Workaround on our side**: score the sentence with one successor word appended and drop the first entry of the answer.

**Request**: write the per-word tags at their own positions (or document the offset), with a test that a model fitted on a trivially learnable tagging gets its own training sentences right.

Issues.Title: Clarify samplingKeyColumnName docs and reject the label as AutoML sampling key
Issues.Body:
Fixes #5567

Users often pass their label column as `samplingKeyColumnName` and expect a stratified split. The sampling key does the opposite: rows that share a key value always land in the same subset, so grouping by the label puts every row of a class on the same side of the split (see #5563).

### Changes

**XML docs (no behavior change)**

One shared wording for `samplingKeyColumnName` on every public API that takes it:

- `DataOperationsCatalog.TrainTestSplit` and `CrossValidationSplit`
- `CrossValidate` / `CrossValidateNonCalibrated` on the binary classification, multiclass classification, regression and clustering catalogs
- `RecommendationCatalog.CrossValidate`, which called the parameter a "stratification column"
- AutoML: `ColumnInformation.SamplingKeyColumnName`, the cross-validation `ExperimentBase.Execute` overload (now points to `ColumnInformation.SamplingKeyColumnName` like its sibling overload) and `AutoMLExperiment.SetDataset`

The new text says what the key is for (keeping related rows, such as all rows from the same user or session, together), says not to use the label column and why, and states that grouping is not stratification. It replaces "This can be used to ensure no label leakage from the train to the test set", which reads like a hint to pass the label.

**AutoML validation**

- `UserInputValidationUtil.ValidateSamplingKey` now throws an `ArgumentException` when the sampling key column is the same as the label column, as suggested in the issue. `ExperimentBase.Execute` calls it before the data is split, so users get this error instead of a generic "all cross validation folds have empty train or test data" failure. No public API is added or changed.
- New test: `UserInputValidationTests.ExecuteThrowsWhenSamplingKeyIsLabel`. It goes through both public `Execute` overloads (train/validate and cross-validation) with a constant label, so every fold would be one-sided if the data were split first.

### Not included

- No check in the core `CrossValidate` methods. They also receive `labelColumnName`, but throwing there would change the behavior of a stable API. I'm happy to add a warning or an exception there if you want it.
- `TrainTestSplit` / `CrossValidationSplit` don't know the label column, so they only get the docs.
- The warning for empty or unbalanced splits mentioned in the issue would need to count rows during the split, so I left it for a separate change.
- `BinaryClassificationExperiment`, `MulticlassClassificationExperiment` and `RegressionExperiment` override `Execute` and currently don't use `SamplingKeyColumnName` at all (see the `TODO` in `BinaryClassificationExperiment.Execute`). The new check therefore applies to the experiments that use `ExperimentBase.Execute` (ranking and recommendation). Making the other experiments respect the sampling key looks like a separate issue; I can open one if that helps.

### Checklist

- [x] Descriptive title
- [x] Associated issue: Fixes #5567
- [x] Public API changes: N/A (XML docs and an internal validation check only)
- [x] The description explains what changed and why
- [x] Tests included for the new validation
